summary: Unexpected 429 spikes when signed-url callbacks and priority-lane decay occur on Dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightEdge reports recurring 429 spikes across multiple API keys after enabling signed-url callback verification and a new priority-lane decay policy on their Dedicated pool. Impact: ~30% request rejection rate for real-time webhook flow; customer reports timeouts and degraded UX for downstream users (search QA). Environment: prod-eu-west, Dedicated pool id dp-82-b, ingress via edge-proxy cluster eu-west-2. Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure warmup + signed-url callbacks on a low-latency priority lane.
2) Send concurrent webhook verification requests (signed URL preflight + callback validation) from 40 parallel workers.
3) Observe sudden 429 responses after ~120s sustained fanout.
Observed behavior: Rapid increase in 429s associated with tenant token-bucket exhaustion. Telemetry shows token usage attributed to callback verification requests and health-check probes; priority-lane decay shortly after warmup correlates with an effective reduction in burst budget. Expected behavior: Signed-url verification should be accounted against separate background/burst pool or marked as low-cost so it does not consume application priority tokens and trigger tenant-wide throttles. Attachments: customer-provided request traces, HAR files, and sample signed-url flow (attached).
steps_to_reproduce: Enable signed-url callbacks and new priority decay on dedicated pool
Initiate 40 parallel webhook signature verification requests
Observe quota and 429 patterns at ~2 minute mark
logs: 2026-03-10T09:14:23Z edge-proxy[proxy-12]: req_id=abc123 signed_url_verify start tenant=brightedge key=rb-** status=200 seq=1
2026-03-10T09:16:07Z rate-limiter[rl-3]: tenant=brightedge tokens_left=0 refill_next=2026-03-10T09:16:10Z action=reject reason=tenant_quota_exhausted
investigation: Support reproduced load pattern in a staging replica using customer's configuration. Metrics show two factors converging: (1) signed-url verification requests originate as short-lived preflight calls that bypass route-level isolation and are charged to the tenant main token pool, and (2) the new priority-lane decay policy reduces available burst credits for the low-latency lane after warmup, causing a net negative burst capacity when healthchecks and callback verifications overlap. Traces link high 'preflight' request rate to the same API key as interactive traffic; ingress NAT re-use contributed to fanout. Dashboards consulted: /dashboards/rate-limiter/tenant-exhaustion, /dashboards/ingress/request-fanout. Hypothesis: accounting misclassification of signed-url callbacks as foreground interactive requests plus priority-lane decay timing causes transient tenant token starvation and 429s.
comments: Maya Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports spikes starting after configuration change; provided traces and HARs.
Jasper Lin (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging with traffic emulator; attaching timeline screenshots to PR#244.
Customer (BrightEdge) 2026-03-11: Can isolate signed-url verification to separate service but prefer platform-level guidance; urgent for EU region SLA.
SRE (Jasper) 2026-03-11: Short-term workaround - instruct client to set signed-url callbacks to use a different API key scoped to background/burst pool; investigating permanent fix.
PD (Rate Limiter) 2026-03-12: Flagged design gap: signed-url verification should be classed as 'low-cost background' with separate quota accounting. Proposing a policy change and a migration runbook.
Support (Maya) 2026-03-12: Submitted escalation to Dedicated product manager and linked INT ticket for config rollout coordination.
partial_findings: Token accounting currently attributes preflight/callback verification to route-level key without background classification
Priority-lane decay reduces burst allowance too aggressively for overlapping healthcheck+callback patterns
Ingress NAT reuse amplifies parallelism from a small set of client IPs
temporary_workarounds: Create separate API key for signed-url callbacks and background workers (scope: background)
Reduce signed-url callback concurrency to <=8 workers as a short-term mitigation
Disable aggressive priority-lane decay flag for the affected Dedicated pool via support toggle
long_term_recommendation: Introduce explicit request-class tagging (interactive | background | healthcheck) at the ingress layer and adjust rate-limiter accounting to separate background/burst pools from interactive token buckets. Update dedicated pool priority-lane decay algorithm to respect ongoing healthcheck and callback windows. Provide a console option to map route paths (e.g., /v1/webhook/callback) to background category.
resolution: Workaround recommended and implemented with customer on 2026-03-11 (separate API key for callbacks). Engineering to deliver policy change: PR created to rate-limiter to add request-class header parsing and background pool accounting (see related PRs). Rolling fix scheduled for 2026-03-20 behind feature flag; post-rollout runbook to validate token accounting. Ticket will remain open until rollout verified in eu-west.
resolution_notes: Customer accepted workaround; observed 98% reduction in 429 within 30 minutes. Monitoring scheduled for two full peak-windows. Follow-up action: product to add 'route-to-background' mapping in console and ops to add a validation check during Dedicated pool config changes.
next_steps: Ship rate-limiter PR to parse request-class header and create background pool accounting
Add console UI to map routes to background category and document best practices for signed-url callbacks
Coordinate rollout with Dedicated customers and schedule verification windows
